look_here_first: Start low on the plant: look for basal leaves plus narrower cauline leaves. Then inspect the sharply pointed strongly ribbed calyx and sunken/pitted glandular hairs.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Low perennial with both basal and cauline leaves, sunken/pitted glandular hairs, conspicuous bracts, and a sharply pointed strongly ribbed calyx.

project_inclusion.range_basis: UT Hays County flora, Travis County Balcones Canyonlands records, and UT Williamson County treatment; no county presence inferred.

morphology_keys.habit: Taprooted perennial with woody caudex, usually short.
morphology_keys.leaves: Both basal and cauline opposite leaves; basal blades narrow oblanceolate to elliptic.
morphology_keys.surface: Leaf surfaces have sunken/pitted glandular hairs.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal raceme with conspicuous leaflike bracts.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Engelmann sage lacks the basal-leaf set and has conspicuous tack-shaped glands. Azure sage is much taller with a long open flowering axis.
